review_receipts.second_editorial_pass: completed: reread all 224 distinct target verse texts, then every one of the 206 explanations against those texts and the actual complete source chapters; correct promised wages versus an unreported completed payment, sought-to-kill wording, and the Hosea speaker attribution
review_receipts.review_method: Work from the exact inventoried verse units and preserve supplied source wording and labels. Read every actual source verse, every retained target and needed context. Retain particular genealogical, narrative, quoted, interpretive, repeated-speech and qualified parallel relationships. Prefix every intrachapter category Same-chapter. Do not impose a per-verse quota or count inventory/technical checks as completed pairs. Keep narrator claims, reported accusations, promises and later theological interpretations distinct.

editorial_notes.note: The supplied Exodus family total is seventy-five, as in the retained Genesis and Acts passages. Deuteronomy explicitly gives seventy; the retained relation identifies a parallel migration account with different totals, not an arithmetical equivalence or independent specialist reconciliation. Maternal household groupings and expanded descendants in Genesis46 retain their own order, names and source wording.

The new king is not assigned a modern historical identity or date. Preserve fortified cities Pithom, Rameses and On, which is City of the Sun, without replacing the list with store cities or proving a new modern site equivalence. The king's military fears are his reported rationale. Midwife Sepphora is not identified with Zipporah merely from similar names. The childbirth killing instruction and expanded river decree remain distinct orders.

Fear of God, refusal to kill and God's good treatment are narrated. The midwives' childbirth explanation remains reported speech, not independently verified obstetric evidence or an unquoted blanket moral ruling. Verse21 says they made houses for themselves; the agency is not replaced with God establishing their houses.

The unnamed Levite parents are linked to explicit later parental genealogies without reconstructing difficult ancestry clauses or substituting another edition's kinship and age details. The unnamed sister receives no new age or name. Preserve three months, the bitumen-pitch basket, marsh placement and Pharaoh's daughter's adoption. Wages are promised; actual payment is not separately narrated.

Stephen's action descriptions, Moses' expectation of recognition and ruler/redeemer reversal remain his retrospective account. Hebrews' faith interpretation remains a later interpretation. No independent legal verdict about the killing, invented medical account of speech, or identification of Hebrews11:27's departure with the initial flight is claimed.

Preserve the seven daughters and Jethro flock wording alongside the return to Reuel. These linked narrative units do not independently establish whether the names are alternate names, different generations or a title. Zipporah, Gershom and the later Eliezer remain as supplied. Gershom's naming explanation is Moses' reported sojourner statement, not a new language-etymology study.

The groaning, ancestral covenant remembrance and divine attention are connected without independently resolving the chronology of all royal-death notices. Verse25 says He became known to them; this is not silently replaced by He knew them. Exodus6:5 retains your covenant rather than an imported alternate pronoun.

Retain Horeb beside Stephen's Sinai label. An angel appears in the bush and the Lord speaks from it; no independent ontological identification of the appearing figure is imposed. The footwear/holy-ground command is compared with Joshua's chief captain without proving that figure's identity. The repeated Moses call and What-is-it response remain intact.

The three Gospel links are distinct actual explicit uses of the ancestral-God declaration in Jesus' resurrection teaching. Each complete retained passage was read, including the surrounding question context; their interpretive application is attributed to Jesus rather than newly derived as an independent specialist conclusion.

The good/spacious milk-and-honey land and supplied seven-peoples lists remain intact. Genesis15 has a longer land-covenant list; no exact list equivalence or new territorial border reconstruction is asserted. The later historical confession is compared on deliverance and destination.

Preserve I am the One Who Is, The One Who Is has sent me, the subsequent Lord-and-ancestral-God message, and the everlasting-name/memorial formula. The later Lord-name disclosure retains its own statement about the patriarchs. No new Hebrew/Greek collation, pronunciation, proposed etymology, or harmonization of every prior-name-knowledge statement is claimed.

The elders' commissioned petition and the later scene naming Moses and Aaron are compared without inventing unlisted participants. Retain the three-day sacrifice request, predicted resistance, strong hand, wonders, Egyptian favour and articles requested. The later source explicitly describes lending and plundering; neither a modern legal classification nor replacement terminology is added. Genesis15:14 retains much baggage.

Moses' serpent sign differs in actor, setting and supplied creature wording from Aaron's later dragon sign. The hand becomes as snow and returns to flesh colour; no leprosy label absent from the Exodus verse or modern diagnosis is inserted. Miriam's explicit leprous-as-snow description remains distinct. The poured-water sign is not equated with the later larger water judgment or given a new physical mechanism.

Preserve weak voice, slow tongue, hard-of-hearing-or-deaf wording and God's promise to open mouths. Aaron will surely speak to Moses in4:14; a fluent-speech claim is not substituted there. The distinct later powerful-in-words account and Jeremiah's youth objection are retained without forced resolution. Moses' matters-pertaining-to-God role and later a-god-to-Pharaoh wording remain distinct delegated-role statements; no ontological equation is independently inferred.

Moses returns toward Egypt with wife and children on beasts of burden. The threat-ended return pattern in Matthew has different people and the opposite destination. Israel's firstborn-son message, Ephraim's firstborn restoration title at the source's Jeremiah38:9 and Hosea's infant-Israel/plural-children wording are compared without replacing them with another numbering or a singular quotation. The release warning retains My people alongside the firstborn language.

Retain angel of the Lord, Zipporah's stone circumcision of her son, falling at the feet, and the twice-stated The blood of my child's circumcision has ceased. No bridegroom-of-blood substitution, assignment of every pronoun or foot-owner, identification of the threatened person or child, medical explanation, or unreported motive is imposed. Circumcision covenant and stone-implement parallels supply stated background, not an independently proven solution of the encounter.

Aaron meets Moses and kisses him; the inner rejoicing anticipated earlier is not separately quoted as a narrated feeling at the meeting. Moses briefs Aaron, the elders assemble, and the actual source assigns both speaking and sign performance to Aaron. The people believe and rejoice, bow and worship. The public-sign notice does not separately enumerate which conditional signs are performed.

actual_read_scope.method: Read the four complete source chapters, all206 retained explanations, and all224 distinct target verse texts. Then checked each proposed connection against both passages, reading the listed further context for quoted speakers, revelation scenes and supplied variants.

peer_review_receipts.source_book_receipt_note: Pinned source identities are carried from the matching curation receipt; the peer review independently read and assessed the actual cached English passages rather than adopting its editorial conclusions.
peer_review_receipts.review_outcome: Approved. No required rationale corrections, pair removals or missing same-chapter labels found.
confirmed_distinctions: Exodus1:5 and Genesis46:27 supply seventy-five, as does Acts7:14; Deuteronomy10:22 supplies seventy. The cross-reference preserves both totals and does not invent a harmonized census or change the source numbers.
The migration family references retain the actual maternal branches and expanded Benjamin wording rather than reordering Exodus or replacing Greek-based genealogical units.
The king's population comparison and proposed wartime risk remain his speech. The narrator's population-growth notices, imposed work and continued increase remain distinct from his stated rationale.
Pithom, Rameses and On/City of the Sun remain actual source wording. The later straw and quota narrative is not projected into the first forced-labour notice.

Sepphora and Puah are the named midwives; no identity with Moses' later wife is inferred. Their reported childbirth explanation is not converted into independently verified obstetric information or a universal approval of every statement.

Exodus1:21 retains they made houses for themselves. It is not rewritten as God building their houses or as an unreported set of named family dynasties; the repeated fear-of-God connection is supported.

The child is hidden for three months with the source's plural agency; the sister is unnamed in the early scene. Later parental genealogies and Stephen/Hebrews interpretations are attributed as later evidence rather than inserted into the original anonymous introduction.
The protected basket placement is not equated with obedience to Pharaoh's killing order. The promised nursing wages are not declared to have been separately narrated as paid.

Stephen's forty-year age, Moses' expectation of recognition as a deliverer, and Hebrews' interpretation of renouncing privilege remain later accounts. They do not erase the Exodus narration of the killing, concealment, fear and flight.

Jethro in Exodus2:16 and Reuel in2:18 remain different supplied names for the daughters' father notices; no extra generation or independently reconstructed genealogy is invented. The well-side Jacob comparison preserves Moses' additional rescue action.
The later two-son account does not make Exodus2:22 deny a second son or identify the child circumcised in4:25. Gershom's foreign-land naming is compared with its explicit later recollection.
Exodus2:25 says He became known to them. The comparisons with3:7 and6:6-7 retain that direction of disclosure rather than replacing it with God knew them.

The angel in the bush, subsequent divine voice, and later chief-captain appearance are not independently identified as one figure. Horeb and the Acts Sinai label remain supplied forms rather than a new geographical reconstruction.

The resurrection uses in Matthew, Mark and Luke are explicitly attributed to Jesus' later quotation and interpretation. The supplied One Who Is, Lord and everlasting memorial formulations remain distinct, and Exodus6:3's prior-name-knowledge statement is not silently harmonized.

The Genesis land-covenant list is not forced into an identical enumeration with Exodus' seven named peoples. The elders' commission and later Moses-and-Aaron petition preserve their actual named participants.
The goods passages retain God-given favour, requested silver/gold/clothing, the Egyptians' lending and the narrative's plunder wording. No different transaction or modern legal conclusion is added.

Moses' serpent-staff scene and Aaron's later dragon-staff scene preserve different performers and supplied creature terms. The limited water-poured-on-ground sign and the later Egyptian river plague are distinct scenes.

Exodus4:6 describes the hand as snow without a leprosy term; Numbers12:10 expressly calls Miriam leprous as snow. The comparison does not add a diagnosis to Moses' hand or claim a modern medical explanation.

Moses' voice-and-tongue objection, Acts7:22's powerful-words assessment and Jeremiah's youth objection remain different descriptions. The promises of opened mouths and words preserve the different intermediaries and audiences.
The two royal-death notices and Matthew's return instruction are compared without reconstructing Egyptian reigns. Moses returns to Egypt whereas Joseph takes the Child from Egypt to Israel.
Jeremiah38:9 retains Ephraim as firstborn; Hosea11:1 retains his children in the plural. The references compare divine-family language without rewriting either as an identical singular quotation.

Exodus4:24 explicitly names an angel of the Lord. The affected him and departure pronouns in4:24-26 are not independently assigned to Moses, the child or a particular foot owner. The circumcision-covenant reference is qualified background, not proof of an unstated target or motive.

Zipporah uses a stone, circumcises her son, falls at the feet and says the blood of her child's circumcision has ceased. The same speech recurs in4:26. No bridegroom-of-blood formula, foreskin-touching act, named child, eight-day age or other edition's speech is inserted.

Exodus4:27 records Aaron's meeting and kiss without separately quoting the inward rejoicing predicted in4:14. Exodus4:30 explicitly gives Aaron both the speaking and sign-performing agency; the links retain that subject and do not enumerate unreported individual signs.
The people's belief, rejoicing and worship answer the visitation-and-affliction message. They are not made evidence that the actual departure from Egypt has already occurred.
peer_review_receipts.source_pronoun_limits: The unresolved identity of the threatened person and pronoun referents in4:24-26 is not adjudicated. The retained relationships are narrative-sequence or explicitly qualified covenant-background comparisons and do not depend on resolving those identities.
peer_review_receipts.limits: AI-assisted English-passage peer QA only. No new Greek/Hebrew, critical-apparatus comparison, independent human-specialist approval or exhaustive discovery claim.

completion_definition: Completed means the initial curated cross-reference pass: the source verse and every listed target passage were read in the pinned Saints-Translation English records, and each retained pair has a specific explanation. It does not mean every possible biblical connection has been exhausted, or independent scholarly approval.
